L28: # Clinical Study for Cats with Mammary Cancer - Information for owners
L29: 
L30: ##
L31: 
L32: ## The care your cat will receive
L33: 
L34: ### Standard surgical care
L35: 
L36: Your cat will undergo routine tumour removal, just like any cat receiving mammary gland surgery at our Veterinary Teaching Hospital.
L37: 
L38: ### Innovative therapy
L39: 
L40: In addition to standard treatment, your cat will receive the investigational therapy (GCN2-IN-6) that will need to be administered orally before and after the surgery.
L41: ### Close monitoring
L42: 
L43: Apart from you as an owner, veterinary specialists will follow your cat throughout the study to ensure their comfort, safety, and well-being.
L44: Preclinical studies at the Small Animal Department demonstrated that this therapy is well-tolerated by cats, with little to no side effects nor with any relevant changes in any blood parameter.
L45: 
L46: ## Benefits and Impact
L47: ### Potential benefit for your cat
L48: 
L49: Participation may help to lower the risk of tumour recurrence and/or tumour spread (metastasis).
L50: The novel drug will be supplied without any additional cost.
L51: 
L52: ### Advancing feline care
L53: 
L54: Your cat’s involvement contributes valuable information toward developing new cancer treatments to increase the life expectancy for cats.
L55: ### Helping humans too
L56: 
L57: The insights gained from this study in cats could pave the way to initiate clinical trials in people with aggressive breast cancers, including TNBC.
L58: 
L59: ## Your Contribution Makes a Difference
L60: 
L61: Without caring owners like you, advancing new treatments to improve the health and lifespan of pets wouldn’t be possible. By participating, you are making a meaningful contribution to advancements in veterinary medicine and helping shape better care for cats, today and in the future.
L62: ### Voluntary participation
L63: 
L64: Participation in this clinical study is completely voluntary. In consultation with the responsible researchers, you may withdraw your cat at any time, without affecting future veterinary care.
L65: 
L66: ### Where the study takes place
L67: 
L68: The study will be conducted at the Veterinary Teaching Hospital of Ghent University, Salisburylaan 133, B-9820 Merelbeke-Melle.
L69: ### Contact information
L70: 
L71: For further information concerning this study, please do not hesitate to contact veterinarian A. Krupa  (adriana.krupa@ugent.be) or Prof. H. de Rooster (hilde.derooster@ugent.be) or contact the reception of the Veterinary Teaching Hospital (+32 9 264 77 00).
